events.title: Linda Leaks and the DC Limited Equity Cooperative Movement Teach-In
events.organization: This event is organized by Jessica "Jess" A. Rucker.hosted by the People's Archive, and supported by the Frederick Dougl
events.short_description: Register to attend this free and intentionally intergenerational learning experience to share in an ongoing movement led by Black women in the decades-old fight for the right to space and place in the nation's capital: https://bit.ly/DCLECTeach-in.
events.full_description: The event seeks to deepen participants’ knowledge of the long and ongoing struggle for safe, decent, and affordable housing in the nation’s capital and will extend access to this critical history at a moment when it has great value, as the nation’s capital continues to be one of the most rapidly gentrifying cities in the United States. Limited equity cooperatives (LECs) became a popular approach to housing justice in DC starting in the late 1970s. In DC, LECs do more than provide cooperatively owned housing affordable to low-income and working-class people; LECs in DC change the material world by reframing housing, democracy, self-determination, and political leadership. The DC LEC movement, from 1978 to 2003, exemplifies how Black women serve as leaders through daily activism and organizing, modeling a literal form of home rule and self-determination in a colonized nation’s capital. This event analyzes LECs in terms of Home Rule and centers a leader of this movement, Linda Leaks–the seasoned Black feminist cooperative educator, activist, and organizer who is known locally as “the Godmother of DC Housing Cooperatives.”

events.title: WPFW 50th Anniversary Gala
events.short_description: An evening honoring five decades of community-powered radio: music, guest speakers, special tributes, and the people who have kept 89.3 on the air since 1977. Tickets on sale in November.
events.full_description:
WPFW turns fifty on February 28, 2027, and this is the night the station marks it. An evening of music, guest speakers and special tributes at Martin's Crosswinds in Greenbelt, Maryland.

Some of the people in that room signed the station on in 1977. Some found 89.3 last week on a car radio. It is the first real chance in a long time to get listeners, volunteers, programmers and staff under one roof.

Tickets go on sale in November. The start time will be announced here and on the air.
